memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He also said to him, "I am the Lord, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to take possession of it." But Abram said, "Sovereign Lord, how can I know that I will gain possession of it?" - Gen 15:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Wait - didn't Abram just believe? Verse 6 declared his faith counted as righteousness, and two verses later he's asking, "How can I know?" Is this a contradiction?

No - it is a comfort. Real faith still asks questions. Abram's belief was genuine, and he still wanted assurance. Faith and questions are not opposites. Doubt that seeks God is not the enemy of faith; it is often faith reaching for firmer ground.

Notice how God responds. He doesn't scold Abram for asking. He doesn't say, "You believed two verses ago, how dare you wonder now." Instead, as we'll see, God graciously gives him a covenant ceremony - visible, unmistakable assurance. God meets honest questions with reassurance, not rebuke.

This should relieve a great many believers. You can be a person of real faith and still have days when you ask, "How can I know?" The father in the Gospels prayed, "I do believe; help me overcome my unbelief!" (Mark 9:24) - and Jesus helped him. Take your questions to God, not away from Him. He is patient with honest seekers, and He delights to give assurance to those who ask.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you feel guilty for having questions alongside your faith?
- Have you taken your doubts to God, or away from Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I do believe - help my unbelief. Thank You that You meet my honest questions with patience, not rebuke. Give me assurance, and hold me steady when I wonder.
Amen.
